title: What the Fire Doesn't Take
logline: After a death, neighbours from a funeral-aid society take over the practical running of the house so the family can sit with their loss.
human_question: Once someone has died, whose work is what is left of their body?

situation.what_happens: A death is announced and a mutual-aid society that people have been paying into for years activates without being asked. Within hours neighbours are doing everything the household cannot: chairs and awnings borrowed, tea made in quantity, notice given, the body attended to, arrangements made, a collection book passed round and a record kept of who gave and who came. The family is deliberately kept out of the work. Over the following days the house fills and empties several times, and eventually the borrowed things go back.
situation.who_is_involved: The bereaved household; the neighbours and society members who do the work; the office-holders who keep the society's book; and the wider set of people for whom attending is itself an obligation.
situation.what_is_at_stake: For the family, being carried through days they could not organise. For the society, the reciprocity it runs on, since everyone there expects the same in their turn. For the neighbourhood, an obligation that is also a ledger, and which quietly records who can be relied on.
situation.how_it_unfolds: These days follow a known sequence, and the sequence is the point: it starts without being requested, peaks, and unwinds. The pressures are cost, distance and relatives travelling. It ends when the borrowed chairs go back and the family is left in a house that has gone quiet. None of it can be scheduled in advance, and nothing about it should be waited for.

concept_merge.why_together: C072 contributes the sources' account of death as a sequence of stoppings in a fixed order, after which nothing in the body is renewed from within and only temperature-born matter continues, so that the body is no longer being lived but only weathered. C070 contributes the reason that is so complete: of the twenty-one kinds of material group, nineteen occur only in living bodies, so what remains is made entirely of the two ordinary kinds also found in stones, water and wind. C063 contributes the inventory in which no item anywhere is called 'owner'. The three say the same thing from three directions, and the society's work is the human answer to it.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: Taken together they explain, without a word of doctrine, why care for the dead is other people's work: nothing is being renewed from inside any more, so everything that happens to the body from now on has to be done to it by somebody. The digest notes that the sources draw no consoling moral from this, and the film should not either. What the situation adds is that a neighbourhood has already organised itself, in advance and by subscription, for exactly that fact.

concept_links.why: The digest sets out the order of cessation, kamma-born matter no longer produced, mind-born and food-born matter fading shortly after, only temperature-born matter continuing, and states plainly that afterwards nothing in the body is renewed from within. Its own words are that the corpse is no longer being lived, only weathered, and that this is why caring for the dead becomes the work of other people.

The digest reports that only two of the twenty-one kinds of material group occur outside living bodies, while the other nineteen, the ones carrying sight, hearing, life, speech and ease of movement, exist only in a living being, so that what remains at the end is made entirely of the two ordinary kinds.

The digest points out that the inventory of twenty-eight kinds contains qualities and processes carefully counted but no item called 'owner', which is the plainest reason why a body, once its own life is not sustaining it, passes into other people's hands.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: These texts describe a body's end as a series of stoppings rather than a single switch. Afterwards nothing in it is renewed from within and only heat and cold keep working on it, which is why everything still to be done for it is done by other people.
what_must_be_real: Explicit, ongoing family consent, given at the time and revocable at any point, including afterwards. The deceased is never filmed without explicit permission. Mourning is never staged, prolonged or repeated, and the doctrine may never be offered to the bereaved as an explanation or a comfort.
position_hint: closing candidate: it is the group's direct answer to what is left of a body once life has gone out of it, and it sets up the question the next stage has to take on.
risks: Intruding on grief; the family decides everything, at the time.
Turning mourning into spectacle, or waiting on a death as an opportunity.
Letting the film settle into 'we return to nature', which the digest says the sources refuse.
The scholastic timing of cessation presented as a clinical account of dying.
drop_if: No family willing to be filmed at such a time.
No society willing to take part, or no access that is not an intrusion.

connections.note: One family answers what remains in the days right after a death; the other watches two bodies answer the same question across a year.
One film watches material being made workable; the other watches material that only the weather works on now.

selection.reason: Used by EPD-0066; the group's closing statement, now also carrying the material-group reason why so little of a body is left once it stops living.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
